conditions.description: The section 14(1)(b) ground presupposes that the person against whom the ground is invoked occupies the legally relevant tenant position vis-à-vis the landlord for the premises.
conditions.scope: Fixed section 14(1)(b) eviction ground; ownership questions outside the tenancy relationship are not independently added as elements.

conditions.exact_rule_quote: sub-let, assigned or otherwise parted with the possession of the whole or any part of the premises
conditions.description: The tenant must have sublet, assigned, or otherwise parted with possession of the whole or any part of the premises.
conditions.scope: The statutory alternatives are treated as alternative modes within one element. The supplied General Radio material confirms broad amplitude, including involuntary sale, but its reported context is limited and is not treated as resolving the present statutory-succession facts.

conditions.exact_rule_quote: on or after the 9th day of June, 1952
conditions.description: The relevant subletting, assignment, or other parting with possession must have occurred on or after 9 June 1952.
conditions.scope: Applies only to the timing of the legally relevant transfer or parting identified under c2.

conditions.exact_rule_quote: without obtaining the consent in writing of the landlord
conditions.description: The qualifying subletting, assignment, or other parting with possession must have occurred without the landlord's written consent.
conditions.scope: Written landlord consent is assessed only if the relevant tenancy and transfer predicates are legally engaged.

bindings.reason: The eviction petition identifies DTC as the lessee/tenant at a stated monthly rent, which is candidate evidence for the tenant predicate but remains an allegation.
The ARCT expressly found a landlord-tenant relationship, providing lower-court support for the tenant predicate without converting that finding into target-court adoption.

bindings.stage: respondents' submissions on Supreme Court appeal
bindings.reason: Respondents disputed the antecedent landlord-tenant relationship, which is candidate evidence against the tenancy chain but is only a submission in the frozen input.
The landlords alleged subletting, assignment, and parting with possession from DTC to MCD; this directly matches the candidate transfer element but remains an allegation.
The ARC found MCD in possession and paying Rs.3500 to DTC as rent, candidate circumstantial support for a transfer or subletting proposition.
The ARC expressly found that DTC had sublet, assigned, or otherwise parted with possession to MCD, directly supporting the candidate element at the lower-court level.
The ARCT found that exclusive possession was handed to MCD and treated that as subletting, providing lower-appellate support for the transfer element.
The High Court expressly found no parting with possession by DTC to MCD and therefore no subletting, directly opposing the candidate element.
The High Court found that the Rs.3500 payment did not itself establish subletting or parting with possession, defeating that particular evidentiary inference for c2.

bindings.stage: respondents' submissions on Supreme Court appeal
bindings.reason: Respondents claimed that MCD retained legal possession all along and that parting with possession had not been proved, candidate opposition to c2 but not a target-court finding.
The eviction petition alleged that the transfer or parting occurred without the appellants' written consent, directly supporting the no-written-consent proposition as an allegation.
The ARC found that respondents did not assert that written consent of the petitioners had been obtained, providing lower-court support for the no-written-consent element.
